descriptors.concept_name: Overview of Income Tax Law in India
descriptors.definition: Income-tax in India is levied and collected under statutory authority derived from the Constitution and enacted legislation. The primary governing statute is the Income-tax Act, 2025, which operates alongside the annual Finance Act and constitutional lists.
inclusion: Levy of direct taxes on income excluding agricultural income
Statutory provisions under the Income-tax Act, 2025
exclusion: Indirect taxes governed by separate constitutional entries
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from indirect taxes and state-levied taxes under the respective constitutional lists.

descriptors.definition: Income-tax is charged on the total income of every person for the tax year at the rates prescribed by the annual Finance Act or the Income-tax Act, 2025. This charging provision forms the foundational basis from which any tax liability legally originates.
inclusion: Total income of persons specified under the Act
Tax rates specified by the Finance Act or Income-tax Act, 2025
exclusion: Incomes explicitly exempt from charge under statutory provisions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from computational provisions by serving strictly as the legal origin of tax liability.

descriptors.definition: Statutory definitions provide precise legal meanings for key terms used throughout the tax legislation. When a term lacks explicit definition in the statute, external aids like the General Clauses Act or dictionaries are utilized.
inclusion: Persons liable to pay tax or refund
Persons subject to assessment proceedings or deemed default
Procedures determining income through various assessment types
exclusion: Ordinary colloquial meanings where statutory definitions explicitly expand or restrict terms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between terms defined directly in Section 2 versus those defined in specific operational sections.

descriptors.definition: Income-tax liability is computed using specified tax rates, augmented by a surcharge levied as a percentage of tax beyond specific income thresholds. Additionally, a Health and Education Cess is applied to the combined total of income-tax and surcharge for all assessees.
inclusion: Concessional tax rates under default regimes
Health and Education Cess at four percent
exclusion: Incomes subject to special tax rates under independent statutory sections
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between base tax rates, progressive surcharges, and the universal health and education cess.
